newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Russia's Lebed meets NATO leaders on expansion.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Lebed meets NATO leaders on expansion.

text.p: Russian security chief Alexander Lebed met NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana at the Western alliance's Brussels headquarters on Monday with a dispute over NATO plans for eastward expansion on the agenda.

The trip is Lebed's first to the West and will give NATO officials a chance to sound out the outspoken former paratroop general who is among the most bitter Russian critics of plans to admit former Kremlin Warsaw Pact allies such as Poland.
The 46-year-old former paratroop commander and Afghan war veteran said on arrival in Brussels on Sunday he had proposals for resolving the dispute, but he gave no details.

He gave a hint, however, that he would have some blunt words for the NATO alliance, which he once described as behaving like a "drunken hooligan" over the expansion plan. He said he expected a "complicated but civilised dialogue".

Lebed was appointed chief security adviser by President Boris Yeltsin on the strength of his performance in the first round of presidential elections this summer. But he has met strong opposition in the government and administration over his tough, independent style.
As a possible successor to Yeltsin, who undergoes heart surgery later this year, he has stirred intense interest among officials and news media alike in the NATO headquarters city.
